The Golden Gate Bridge, completed in 1937, stretches 8,981 feet across the entrance to San Francisco Bay, linking the city to Marin County. Its two 746-foot-tall Art Deco towers and signature International Orange color make it one of the most photographed suspension bridges in the world. From its groundbreaking in 1933 to its opening in May 1937, the bridge represented a monumental engineering achievement, holding the title of the world’s longest suspension span until 1964.

Recognized as both a California Historical Landmark and a San Francisco Designated Landmark, the bridge continues to draw millions of visitors each year. Its elegant cables and sweeping vistas of the Pacific Ocean and city skyline underscore its status as an enduring icon of California’s coastal landscape.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Golden Gate Bridge’s striking International Orange towers rise above the deep blue waters of San Francisco Bay, connected by a network of suspension cables. Vehicles traverse the six-lane roadway, flanked by pedestrian walkways, as the bridge links the city to Marin County. In the distance, the urban skyline and verdant hills complete the iconic vista.

A recent engineering retrofit of the west railing introduced thinner slats that emit wind-induced screeching tones during high winds. After wind-tunnel tests, engineers developed U-shaped clips with rubber inserts to dampen vibrations on all 12,000 slats. This $450,000 solution is set for installation in early 2023, promising to silence the bridge’s unintended song.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Golden Gate Bridge, painted in its signature International Orange, spans the entrance to San Francisco Bay, connecting the city to Marin County. Two massive towers rise 227 meters above the water, supporting nearly 2.8 kilometers of roadway with a network of suspension cables. Under a clear blue sky, the bridge’s vivid color contrasts sharply with the deep blue of the bay and the muted greens and browns of the surrounding hills.

Completed in 1937 after four years of construction, the bridge remains a vital transportation link and a world-renowned landmark. Dedicated walkways allow pedestrians and cyclists to traverse the span during daylight hours, and nearby rental shops make it easy to explore the structure on two wheels. The Golden Gate Bridge’s elegant design and striking color continue to draw photographers, tourists, and engineering enthusiasts from around the globe.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
